newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission to decide method of setting sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Commission to decide method of setting sanctions.

text.p: The European Commission will on Wednesday decide on a method for calculating financial penalties which can under the Maastricht Treaty be imposed on member states for failing to implement Court of Justice rulings.
The move follows a Commission decision taken last May on the principle of applying sanctions when member states fail to comply with European Court of Justice rulings in infringement proceedings.

The possibility of financial penalties is provided for under Article 171 paragraph 2 of the EU Treaty as amended by Maastricht, but so far the Commission has not used the possibility and needs a coherent approach to setting the penalties, Commission spokeswoman Betty Olivi said.
The Commission is expected to determine a method -- based on a percentage of GDP -- which would then be adapted to the seriousness and length of the infringement, EU officials said.
"We will tomorrow define the methods of calculating the financial penalties," said Commission spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida. "It is not a question tomorrow of defining or treating specific cases."
The move confirms the Commission's determination to clamp down on non-respect by member states of EU law.
The EU has a three-stage infringement procedure, starting with a warning letter, going on to a reasoned opinion and in the last instance referral to the Court of Justice.

In December, the Commission, for example, sent Greece a reasoned opinion for failing to open up private schools, while Italy was referred to the Court of Justice for failing to transpose into national law rules on transport of polluting goods by sea.
Vale de Almeida said the rules agreed by the Commission on Wednesday would not be retroactive.
In the future the Commission would inform the Court of Justice of the proposed sanction at the time of referral.
